title: Runtime negotiate: speculative decoder with cost-aware routing and acceptance calibrator
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a runtime component that negotiates speculative decoding across model variants with a cost-aware routing function and an acceptance calibrator. The component will: 1) compute a lightweight cost/latency score for candidate model kernels (kernel price function), 2) run a short prefill calibration probe to produce an early acceptance probability, and 3) choose between fast speculative decode branches with an explicit fallback plan to ensure correctness and latency SLOs. Scope: routing logic, acceptance metric definitions/collection, integration hooks with kernel selection and prefill scheduler, fallback playbook, and observability. Non-goals: model architecture changes, beam search algorithm redesign, or changes to customer-facing API surface (those will be separate PRs).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes routing decision trace per request containing: chosen model variant, kernel fingerprint, cost_score, acceptance_prob, and fallback_reason (if any)
Acceptance calibrator demonstrates <1% false-accept rate and <0.5% false-reject rate on synthetic eval set (see links) at default threshold
End-to-end median tail latency better or equal to baseline for 95% of requests and reduced token compute cost for top 40% of traffic mix
Clear rollback path: can toggle speculative routing off via feature flag per-POOL without restart
Integration tests cover kernel-aware routing when models with incompatible kernels are in the candidate set
Telemetry dashboard surfaces acceptance distribution, fallback frequency, and per-kernel throughput with 2x retention compared to default
implementation_notes: Design decisions so far: 1) Kernel-aware routing: generate a 64-bit kernel fingerprint at model load and annotate candidate descriptors. Routing cost uses benchmark-derived throughput_peeks and latency_percentiles to compute a kernel_price = alpha * expected_latency + beta * token_cost. 2) Acceptance calibrator: run a lightweight k-token prefill probe (k configurable, default 6) using the candidate fast-decoder; acceptance probability is computed via a logistic model trained on historical prefill vs final-token agreement. 3) Thresholding: allow per-customer and per-route adjustments; introduce a grace window (N tokens) where acceptance threshold is relaxed linearly to favor latency. 4) Fallback: warm hotstandby pool with last-known-good quantized variant; fallback sequence is: speculative fast-decoder -> fallback to warm standby -> final fallback to canonical model. 5) Safety: when kernel incompatibility detected, skip speculative branch and mark decision as SKIP_KERNEL_MISMATCH. 6) Scheduling: prefill probes scheduled in the prefill phase and piggybacked on existing KV cache warming to avoid extra memory pressure.
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Spike completed for kernel fingerprinting prototype. Microbenchmarks show kernel fingerprint generation ~120us per model on init.
2026-03-02: Acceptance calibrator prototype (logistic reg) trained on 50k labeled prefill->final pairs. Initial ROC AUC 0.92.
2026-03-05: Integrated routing trace into request context. Hooked into tracing pipeline (trace id instrumentation complete).
2026-03-09: End-to-end lab run (traffic replay) against runtime-2.3 baseline: 18% of requests eligible for speculative fast branch, token cost reduced by 9% for those requests, fallback rate 3.6%.
2026-03-12: Feature-flag gating and per-pool toggles implemented. Preparing PR for code review and adding QA matrix.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi): validate customer-impact metric; add per-customer opt-out and conservative default thresholds

Design (Clara): add UI fields for threshold tuning on console and include confidence histogram in rollout dashboard
Infra (Noah): confirm warm standby pool sizing strategy to avoid OOMs under bursty traffic; suggested soft limit and eviction policy
qa_plan: Unit tests for kernel fingerprinting and kernel_price computation with synthetic kernel metrics
Integration test: gated candidate set where fast-decoder has incompatible kernel -> assert speculative skipped and trace flagged
Replay test: run 1M historical requests through the negotiator vs baseline; assert fallback frequency <5% and no crash
Chaos test: induce slow prefill probe and validate graceful backoff to canonical model without request timeouts
A/B experiment plan for canary rollout across 2% -> 10% -> 50% traffic with rollback thresholds defined
risks_mitigation: Risk: Acceptance model overfits to training corpus -> Mitigation: continuous online calibration using streaming labelled signals and weekly re-eval
Risk: Warm standby increases memory footprint -> Mitigation: autoscale warm pool and implement LRU eviction for cold model variants
Risk: Kernel mismatch causes increased CPU overhead -> Mitigation: perform cheap compatibility check early and document skip-path with metrics
Risk: Customer regressions due to aggressive thresholds -> Mitigation: conservative defaults and per-customer rollback toggle
